name: John Marshall Bank
area: Northern Virginia, Washington, D.C. and suburban Maryland
title: John Marshall Bank SBA Loans & Rates (VA)
description: John Marshall Bank (Reston, VA) SBA loan rates: current 7(a) caps with prime at 7.00%, how this D.C.-area business bank lends, and what to ask first.
lede: John Marshall Bank is a Reston, Virginia business bank that lends to companies and professionals across the Washington, D.C. region.
about: John Marshall Bank is a commercial bank headquartered in Reston, Virginia. It is the banking subsidiary of John Marshall Bancorp, which trades on Nasdaq. The bank has built its business around relationship banking for local companies, professional practices, nonprofits and real estate investors rather than a large consumer branch network.

Its offices are concentrated in Northern Virginia, Washington, D.C. and Montgomery County, Maryland. In September 2026 John Marshall Bancorp agreed to combine with Eagle Financial Services, the parent of Bank of Clarke, in a deal expected to close in early 2027. Both bank brands are expected to stay in use, and the merger would extend the footprint west into the Shenandoah Valley.

Typical clients include government contractors, law and medical practices, accounting firms, property owners and family-owned service companies. For an SBA borrower, that means a lender used to cash-flow-based commercial credit and owner-occupied real estate in one of the most expensive property markets in the country. Deposit relationships usually come with the loan, so expect the bank to ask for your operating accounts as part of the deal.
sba_fit: In the D.C. market, the most common SBA use with a bank like John Marshall is buying a practice or service business, where a 7(a) loan can stretch repayment to 10 years and limit the down payment. Owner-occupied office or flex space is the other big one: a 504 loan, with the bank in first position and a Virginia or Maryland CDC on the second lien, can lock in a long fixed rate on a pricey building. Government contractors with receivables can also ask about SBA working capital lines.
known_for: Pending combination with Bank of Clarke parent Eagle Financial

faqs.q: Does John Marshall Bank make SBA loans?
faqs.a: John Marshall Bank appears in SBA lending data as a participating lender. Ask its business bankers which programs they offer today, whether they hold Preferred Lender status for faster approvals, and whether they handle 504 first liens alongside a local CDC.

faqs.q: Where does John Marshall Bank lend?
faqs.a: The bank is based in Reston, Virginia and focuses on Northern Virginia, Washington, D.C. and suburban Maryland. Businesses outside that region can still ask, but community banks usually prefer borrowers they can visit and serve with a local relationship manager.

faqs.q: Is John Marshall Bank merging with Bank of Clarke?
faqs.a: In September 2026 John Marshall Bancorp agreed to combine with Eagle Financial Services, parent of Bank of Clarke. The deal was expected to close in early 2027 pending approvals, with both bank names kept. A loan in process should not be affected, but ask your banker about timing.

The bank changed its name to Lake Ridge Bank as it grew beyond the city of Monona itself.

The bank's offices are concentrated in Madison and surrounding Dane County communities. That keeps its lending focused on the greater Madison economy, which mixes state government, university-linked companies, health care, construction trades, restaurants and a steady stream of owner-operated service businesses. Lenders know the local market well, from east side retail corridors to the light industrial parks around Madison, and can judge Dane County property values without outside help.

Lake Ridge serves business clients alongside consumers, with commercial loans, owner-occupied real estate financing, equipment loans, lines of credit and treasury services. Borrowers who banked with Monona Bank keep the same institution, just under the newer name. sba_fit: A Dane County owner would most likely use Lake Ridge Bank for a 7(a) loan to buy an existing local business, such as a restaurant, trade contractor or clinic, where the seller is retiring and collateral is thin. Madison commercial space is not cheap, and a 504 loan, with the bank on the first lien and a Wisconsin CDC on the second, keeps the down payment near 10%. Commercial and owner-occupied real estate loans

name: St. Mary's Bank
title: St. Mary's Bank SBA Loans & Rates (NH)
description: St. Mary's Bank, the Manchester NH credit union, and SBA loan rates: 7(a) caps with prime at 7.00%, business lending basics, and questions to ask first.
lede: St. Mary's Bank is a member-owned credit union in Manchester, New Hampshire, widely recognized as the first credit union in the United States.
about: Despite the word bank in its name, St. Mary's Bank is a credit union. It was founded in 1908 in Manchester, New Hampshire, by French-Canadian mill workers and parishioners of St. Mary's parish, under the name La Caisse Populaire Ste-Marie. It is commonly cited as the first credit union in the United States.

Today it is a member-owned financial cooperative serving Manchester and communities across southern New Hampshire. Membership is open to people who live or work in its eligible area, and business owners can join to open business accounts and apply for commercial credit. As a cooperative, it returns value to members through rates and fees rather than to outside shareholders, and its decisions are made locally in Manchester.

St. Mary's Bank offers business checking, commercial real estate loans, equipment and vehicle loans, and lines of credit to local small businesses. Its business clients tend to be owner-operated firms in the Manchester and Merrimack Valley area, such as contractors, retailers, restaurants and professional offices. Loans tend to be modest in size, and the credit union generally wants to see the business's operating accounts held there as well.
sba_fit: For a Manchester-area business, an SBA loan through a credit union like St. Mary's Bank is most useful when a conventional commercial loan falls short on down payment or term. Common cases are buying a building for your own business, refinancing equipment, or funding working capital with a longer payback. Credit unions face caps on member business lending, so larger or more complex deals may be routed to the SBA structure or to a partner. Expect membership to be required before you apply.
known_for: Widely cited as the first US credit union, founded 1908
Business accounts and commercial loans for members

faqs.q: Is St. Mary's Bank a bank or a credit union?
faqs.a: St. Mary's Bank is a credit union, owned by its members, even though its name says bank. It began in Manchester, New Hampshire in 1908 and is widely recognized as the first credit union in the country. Deposits are insured by the NCUA rather than the FDIC.

faqs.q: Does St. Mary's Bank make SBA loans?
faqs.a: St. Mary's Bank appears in SBA lending data as a participating lender. Ask its business lending team which SBA programs are available now, the loan sizes it prefers, and whether you must become a member before applying. Most credit unions require membership.

faqs.q: Can I get an SBA loan at a credit union in Manchester NH?
faqs.a: Yes, some credit unions are approved SBA lenders, and St. Mary's Bank is one Manchester option to ask. Rates are capped by the SBA the same way they are at banks. Compare its offer with a local bank and, for real estate, a 504 loan through a New Hampshire CDC.

Commercial real estate and small business loans

faqs.q: Does Hanover Community Bank NY offer SBA loans?

title: PCB Bank SBA Loans & Rates (CA)
description: PCB Bank (formerly Pacific City Bank, Los Angeles) SBA loan rates: 7(a) caps with prime at 7.00%, how its SBA team lends, and questions to ask first.
lede: PCB Bank, formerly Pacific City Bank, is a Los Angeles Koreatown bank with an active SBA lending business.
about: PCB Bank is a commercial bank headquartered in Los Angeles, in the Koreatown area. It was founded as Pacific City Bank and later shortened its name to PCB Bank. Its holding company, PCB Bancorp, trades on Nasdaq. It operates as a business-focused commercial bank and is one of the larger Korean-American banks in the United States.

The bank grew up serving the Korean-American business community in Southern California and has since added branches and loan production offices in other states with large Korean-American populations. Several of its lending offices focus on SBA and commercial real estate loans rather than deposits. That network lets it serve borrowers well outside Los Angeles.

Its business clients include restaurants, retailers, wholesalers, gas stations, hotels and motels, and owners of commercial property. Many are first- or second-generation immigrant entrepreneurs, and staff can often work with borrowers in Korean as well as English. Bankers are used to cash-intensive businesses and to deals where a buyer is purchasing a business from another member of the same community.
sba_fit: PCB Bank is a common choice for buying an existing small business, such as a restaurant, liquor store, dry cleaner or motel, where a 7(a) loan covers business value that a conventional loan will not. It is also used for owner-occupied commercial real estate, either through a 7(a) real estate loan with a 25-year term or a 504 structure. Borrowers who prefer to work in Korean may find the process easier here. Compare its rate and fees with at least one other SBA lender before committing.

faqs.q: Does PCB Bank offer SBA loans?
faqs.a: Yes, SBA lending is a core business line for PCB Bank, and it appears in SBA data as an active lender. Ask its SBA team which programs fit your deal, whether it can approve under Preferred Lender authority, and the rate and fees for your loan size.

faqs.q: Is PCB Bank the same as Pacific City Bank?
faqs.a: Yes. PCB Bank is the Los Angeles bank originally called Pacific City Bank. It shortened its name, and its parent company is PCB Bancorp. Older documents and reviews may still use the Pacific City Bank name.

faqs.q: Can PCB Bank help with an SBA loan in Korean?
faqs.a: PCB Bank was built around the Korean-American business community, and many of its bankers work with clients in Korean and English. Ask the branch or loan office near you. SBA loan documents themselves are in English.

name: Canyon View Credit Union
area: Salt Lake County and nearby Utah counties
title: Canyon View Credit Union SBA Loans (UT)
description: Canyon View Federal Credit Union (formerly University First) SBA loan rates: 7(a) caps with prime at 7.00%, business lending in Utah, and what to ask.
h1: Canyon View Credit Union SBA loans (UT)
lede: Canyon View Federal Credit Union is a Salt Lake City credit union that operated for decades as University First Federal Credit Union.
about: Canyon View Federal Credit Union is a member-owned credit union headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah. For many years it was University First Federal Credit Union, often called UFirst, and it grew up on and around the University of Utah campus. It changed its name to Canyon View as it broadened its membership beyond the university community.

Membership now covers people who live or work in Salt Lake County and several surrounding counties. The credit union runs branches across the Salt Lake Valley and has extended into other parts of the state, including St. George. It describes itself as having around two dozen branches, and members can also use shared credit union branches and ATMs.

Alongside consumer accounts and loans, Canyon View offers business checking and business lending for members. Its business borrowers are mostly small, owner-operated companies along the Wasatch Front, from contractors and retailers to professional services firms. Business lending is a smaller part of the credit union than consumer lending, so owners should ask early about loan sizes and the documents needed.
sba_fit: For a Salt Lake Valley business, an SBA loan through a credit union like Canyon View makes most sense for a modest, straightforward need: equipment, working capital, refinancing higher-cost debt, or buying a small owner-occupied space. The SBA guarantee lets a credit union say yes to a longer term or smaller down payment than its standard business loan. Larger acquisitions or construction projects may be better suited to a bank with a dedicated SBA team, or to a 504 loan through a Utah CDC. Membership is required.
known_for: Formerly University First Federal Credit Union (UFirst)
Roots at the University of Utah
Branches across the Salt Lake Valley

faqs.q: Is Canyon View Credit Union the same as University First?
faqs.a: Yes. Canyon View Federal Credit Union is the Salt Lake City credit union formerly named University First Federal Credit Union, or UFirst. It changed its name as membership expanded beyond the University of Utah community. Member accounts carried over to the new name.

faqs.q: Does Canyon View Federal Credit Union offer SBA loans?
faqs.a: Canyon View appears in SBA lending data as a participating lender. Ask its business lending staff whether SBA loans are offered today, what loan sizes they handle, and how long approval takes. Smaller credit union SBA programs often focus on simpler loans.

faqs.q: Who can join Canyon View Credit Union for a business loan?
faqs.a: Membership is generally open to people who live or work in Salt Lake County and certain nearby Utah counties, and to their businesses. You will need to join before a loan closes. Ask the credit union to confirm your eligibility at the start.

name: Bravera Bank
title: Bravera Bank SBA Loans & Rates (ND)
description: Bravera Bank (formerly American Bank Center, Dickinson ND) SBA loan rates: 7(a) caps with prime at 7.00%, ag and business lending, and what to ask first.
lede: Bravera Bank is a Dickinson, North Dakota bank, known until 2021 as American Bank Center, that lends to farms, ranches and businesses across the region.
about: Bravera Bank is a community bank headquartered in Dickinson, in western North Dakota. It operated as American Bank Center until June 2021, when it announced the Bravera name. Before that, the institution had used earlier names including Bank Center First, based in Bismarck. The new name was chosen to unite the bank and its affiliated businesses under one brand.

Bravera's branches are spread across North Dakota, from the Bakken and western ranch country to Bismarck and other central and eastern communities, with locations in neighboring states as well. The Bravera brand also covers related insurance and wealth businesses. Most of its markets are small towns where the local bank is a key source of business credit.

Agriculture is a large part of its customer base, alongside small and mid-size businesses tied to energy, construction, trucking, retail and health care. That mix means lenders are used to cyclical cash flow and weather-driven revenue swings. Its bankers generally know local markets and families well, which can matter when a small-town business changes hands.
sba_fit: In North Dakota, an SBA loan through Bravera is likely to support a main street or energy-related business rather than a farm, since most farm credit runs through conventional or FSA programs. Typical uses are buying a business in a small town where few buyers have large down payments, building or buying a shop or warehouse, or financing trucks and heavy equipment over a longer term. For owner-occupied real estate, ask about a 504 loan with a North Dakota CDC.
known_for: Business lending tied to energy and construction
Related insurance and wealth services under the Bravera name

faqs.q: Is Bravera Bank the same as American Bank Center?
faqs.a: Yes. Bravera Bank is the Dickinson, North Dakota bank that was called American Bank Center until it announced its new name in June 2021. Customers kept their accounts and loans, and the bank's lending focus on businesses and agriculture continued.

faqs.q: Does Bravera Bank offer SBA loans?
faqs.a: Bravera Bank appears in SBA lending data as a participating lender. Ask a business banker which SBA programs it actively offers, whether it handles 504 first liens with a North Dakota CDC, and how long approvals usually take.

faqs.q: Can I use an SBA loan for a farm or ranch?
faqs.a: SBA loans can fund some agricultural businesses, but many farm and ranch loans go through conventional bank programs or the USDA Farm Service Agency instead. A lender like Bravera can tell you which option fits your operation and whether SBA rules allow it.

name: Busey Bank
area: Illinois, Missouri, Indiana, Florida and the central and southwestern US
title: Busey Bank SBA Loans & Rates (IL)
description: Busey Bank (Champaign, IL) SBA loan rates: 7(a) caps with prime at 7.00%, how this Illinois-based regional bank lends after CrossFirst, and what to ask.
lede: Busey Bank is an Illinois-born regional bank that now lends from the Midwest to Florida and, since its CrossFirst merger, into the Southwest.
about: Busey Bank is the bank subsidiary of First Busey Corporation, which traces its roots to Urbana, Illinois in the 1800s. The bank is headquartered in Champaign, Illinois, and remains one of the best-known banks in central Illinois. Busey grew from a single Champaign-Urbana bank into a regional institution while keeping its headquarters in the area.

Busey has expanded through acquisitions, adding banks in the St. Louis area, the Chicago suburbs and southwest Florida. In March 2025 it completed its merger with CrossFirst Bankshares of Leawood, Kansas, bringing in offices in Kansas, Missouri, Oklahoma, Texas, Colorado, Arizona and New Mexico. Each deal brought new customers and local bankers into the Busey network.

The bank serves consumers, businesses and wealth management clients. Its commercial lending covers owner-occupied and investor real estate, middle-market companies, and small businesses, with treasury management and payment services through its FirsTech subsidiary. Small business clients typically work with a local banker, with specialists brought in for treasury or larger credits.
sba_fit: Busey's size and spread make it a reasonable option for SBA loans in several quite different markets. In central Illinois and St. Louis, that often means a 7(a) loan to buy a local business or a 504 loan for a building. In growth markets inherited from CrossFirst, such as Dallas, Phoenix or Denver, owners may use SBA financing to buy property or fund expansion with less cash down. Ask whether SBA loans are handled by a central team or by your local banker.
known_for: Offices from Illinois and Florida to the Southwest

faqs.q: Does Busey Bank offer SBA loans?
faqs.a: Busey Bank appears in SBA lending data as a participating lender. Ask a business banker which SBA programs it offers in your market, whether it can approve under Preferred Lender authority, and how its process works across its newer offices.

faqs.q: What happened to CrossFirst Bank?
faqs.a: CrossFirst Bankshares, based in Leawood, Kansas, merged into First Busey in March 2025, and CrossFirst Bank became part of Busey Bank. Former CrossFirst clients in Kansas, Oklahoma, Texas, Colorado, Arizona and New Mexico now bank with Busey.

faqs.q: What SBA rate could Busey Bank offer?
faqs.a: Busey sets the rate, but SBA caps apply. With prime at 7.00%, variable 7(a) maximums run from 10.00% on loans over $350,000 to 13.50% on loans of $50,000 or less. For real estate, compare a 504 loan, where the debenture rate was about 6.57% in November 2026.

name: Coastal States Bank
area: Lowcountry South Carolina, Savannah, Atlanta and SBA borrowers nationwide
title: Coastal States Bank SBA Loans & Rates (SC)
description: Coastal States Bank (Hilton Head, SC) SBA loan rates: 7(a) caps with prime at 7.00%, how its national SBA lending team works, and what to ask first.
lede: Coastal States Bank is a Hilton Head Island community bank that also runs a national SBA and government-guaranteed lending team.
about: Coastal States Bank is headquartered on Hilton Head Island, South Carolina. Its community banking offices are in Hilton Head and Bluffton, and it also serves Savannah and metro Atlanta. Locally, it lends to businesses, professionals and real estate owners in the Lowcountry. It is a relatively young bank compared with many community banks in the Southeast.

Beyond its home market, the bank operates a Government Guaranteed Lending group that makes SBA loans to borrowers across the country, with lenders based in several regions. It received SBA Preferred Lender status in 2018, which lets it approve qualifying SBA loans without sending each file to the SBA. Its lenders work across many industries.

That combination means two kinds of clients: local Lowcountry businesses that want a hometown bank, and owners elsewhere who find Coastal States specifically for SBA financing. For the second group, the draw is a lender that does government-guaranteed loans every day. Those borrowers often never visit a branch, working instead with an SBA lender assigned to their region.
sba_fit: Coastal States is set up for borrowers who want a lender that does SBA loans regularly, even if the business is nowhere near Hilton Head. Typical uses include buying an existing business, purchasing or building owner-occupied property, and funding expansion with a 7(a) loan. Preferred Lender status can shorten approval time. Because its SBA team lends nationally, you may work mostly by phone and email with a regional lender. Compare its quote with a local bank and a 504 loan through your state's CDC.
known_for: Community offices in Hilton Head and Bluffton

faqs.q: Does Coastal States Bank make SBA loans outside South Carolina?
faqs.a: Yes. Coastal States Bank describes itself as a national SBA lender, and its Government Guaranteed Lending team works with borrowers in many states. Ask which lender covers your region, which programs fit your deal, and how much of the process can be done remotely.

faqs.q: Is Coastal States Bank an SBA Preferred Lender?
faqs.a: Coastal States Bank received SBA Preferred Lender Program status in 2018. Preferred Lenders can approve eligible loans under delegated authority, which usually speeds up the process. Confirm current status and expected timelines with the bank when you apply.

faqs.q: Where is Coastal States Bank located?
faqs.a: Coastal States Bank is headquartered on Hilton Head Island, South Carolina, with a community office in Bluffton. It also serves Savannah, Georgia and the Atlanta area, and its SBA lenders are based in several parts of the country.

name: Falcon National Bank
area: central Minnesota and the Twin Cities area
title: Falcon National Bank SBA Loans (MN)
description: Falcon National Bank (Minnesota) SBA loan rates: 7(a) caps with prime at 7.00%, how this central Minnesota and Twin Cities bank lends, and what to ask.
lede: Falcon National Bank is a Minnesota community bank serving businesses in central Minnesota and the northern Twin Cities area.
about: Falcon National Bank is a national bank chartered in Minnesota, with its main office in Foley, east of St. Cloud. It also has a significant presence in St. Cloud and has expanded toward the Twin Cities, including Maple Grove and the north metro. It is a relatively young bank compared with many Minnesota community banks.

Its footprint covers central Minnesota towns and the northern and western Twin Cities suburbs, a region with a mix of manufacturing, agriculture, construction, health care and small retail and service businesses. Many of these companies are family-owned, and ownership transitions are common as founders retire, which creates steady demand for acquisition and real estate financing.

Falcon focuses on business banking, with commercial real estate, equipment, working capital and construction loans plus treasury services. It positions itself around local decision making for owner-operated companies rather than a large consumer franchise. Owners can expect to deal directly with a lender who knows their market and can explain what the bank needs.
sba_fit: A central Minnesota owner might use Falcon National Bank for a 7(a) loan to buy a small manufacturer, contractor or service company from a retiring owner, or to combine a building and equipment in one longer-term loan. In the growing north metro, a 504 loan, with Falcon on the first mortgage and a Minnesota CDC on the second, can help buy or build owner-occupied space with around 10% down. Ask how SBA loans are handled and whether the bank approves them in-house.
known_for: Presence in St. Cloud and the north Twin Cities
Commercial real estate and equipment lending

faqs.q: Does Falcon National Bank offer SBA loans?
faqs.a: Falcon National Bank appears in SBA lending data as a participating lender. Ask its commercial lenders which SBA programs it uses today, typical loan sizes, and whether it partners with a Minnesota CDC as the first-lien lender on 504 projects.

faqs.q: Where is Falcon National Bank located?
faqs.a: Falcon National Bank's main office is in Foley, Minnesota, near St. Cloud. It also has offices in the St. Cloud area and the northern and western Twin Cities suburbs, such as Maple Grove. Confirm the nearest office before you apply.

faqs.q: What rate does Falcon National Bank charge on SBA loans?
faqs.a: The bank sets your rate within SBA limits. With prime at 7.00%, variable 7(a) caps range from 10.00% on loans over $350,000 to 13.50% on loans of $50,000 or less. Fixed rates are also allowed under separate SBA caps.

name: Heritage Bank
title: Heritage Bank SBA Loans & Rates (WA)
description: Heritage Bank SBA loan rates (Olympia, WA): 7(a) caps with prime at 7.00%, how this Pacific Northwest bank lends after the Kitsap Bank merger, and more.
lede: Heritage Bank is an Olympia, Washington commercial bank serving businesses across the Pacific Northwest.
about: Heritage Bank is headquartered in Olympia, Washington. It is the bank subsidiary of Heritage Financial Corporation, which trades on Nasdaq. Many other banks share the Heritage name, so make sure you are looking at the Olympia-based one. It is one of the larger community banks based in the Puget Sound region.

Heritage has grown through mergers. In 2014 it combined with Washington Banking Company, parent of Whidbey Island Bank, and it has acquired other Puget Sound banks since. On January 31, 2026 it completed its acquisition of Olympic Bancorp, and Kitsap Bank merged into Heritage Bank. Kitsap Bank's 16 branches on the Kitsap Peninsula continue to operate under the Kitsap Bank name as part of Heritage.

Its branches now cover western Washington and the Puget Sound, plus parts of Oregon and Idaho. Commercial lending is the core of the business, including owner-occupied real estate, business lines of credit, equipment loans and SBA lending. Small businesses generally work with local relationship bankers, with specialists for treasury and larger loans.
sba_fit: In the Puget Sound and Pacific Northwest, an SBA loan from Heritage Bank is often used to buy owner-occupied property, where a 504 or 25-year 7(a) real estate loan keeps the down payment and payments manageable in a high-cost market. It is also a fit for buying an existing business, from marine trades on Kitsap and Whidbey to professional practices in Olympia and Tacoma. Ask whether the bank has a dedicated SBA team and Preferred Lender authority for faster approval.
known_for: Merged with Whidbey Island Bank's parent in 2014
Branches in Washington, Oregon and Idaho

faqs.q: Does Heritage Bank in Olympia offer SBA loans?
faqs.a: Heritage Bank of Olympia, Washington appears in SBA lending data as a participating lender and lists SBA loans among its business products. Ask a business banker which programs it offers today, the loan sizes it prefers, and whether it can approve under Preferred Lender authority.

faqs.q: Is Kitsap Bank part of Heritage Bank now?
faqs.a: Yes. Heritage Financial completed its acquisition of Olympic Bancorp on January 31, 2026, and Kitsap Bank merged into Heritage Bank. The Kitsap branches still use the Kitsap Bank name, but they are part of Heritage Bank. Earlier, in 2014, Whidbey Island Bank also became part of Heritage.

faqs.q: Which Heritage Bank is this?
faqs.a: This page covers Heritage Bank headquartered in Olympia, Washington, the subsidiary of Heritage Financial Corporation. It is not related to the many other banks named Heritage in other states. Check the headquarters city before you apply.
